name: Find the Car
description: Timur is in a car traveling on the number line from point $$$0$$$ to point $$$n$$$. The car starts moving from point $$$0$$$ at minute $$$0$$$. There are $$$k+1$$$ signs on the line at points $$$0, a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$, and Timur knows that the car will arrive there at minutes $$$0, b_1, b_2, \dots, b_k$$$, respectively. The sequences $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ are strictly increasing with $$$a_k = n$$$. Between any two adjacent signs, the car travels with a constant speed . Timur has $$$q$$$ queries: each query will be an integer $$$d$$$, and Timur wants you to output how many minutes it takes the car to reach point $$$d$$$, rounded down to the nearest integer .
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$, and $$$q$$$, ($$$k \leq n \leq 10^9$$$; $$$1 \leq k, q \leq 10^5$$$) — the final destination, the number of points Timur knows the time for, and the number of queries respectively. The second line of each test case contains $$$k$$$ integers $$$a_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$; $$$a_i \lt a_{i+1}$$$ for every $$$1 \leq i \leq k-1$$$; $$$a_k = n$$$). The third line of each test case contains $$$k$$$ integers $$$b_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq b_i \leq 10^9$$$; $$$b_i \lt b_{i+1}$$$ for every $$$1 \leq i \leq k-1$$$). Each of the following $$$q$$$ lines contains a single integer $$$d$$$ ($$$0 \leq d \leq n$$$) — the distance that Timur asks the minutes passed for. The sum of $$$k$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$10^5$$$, and the sum of $$$q$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each query, output a single integer — the number of minutes passed until the car reaches the point $$$d$$$, rounded down.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1971E — Find the Car [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
